title: edgewit bank file
description: A single bank file: one domain, many edge cases.

domain.description: Dotted path matching the file location, e.g. backend/rest-api/pagination

side.description: Must agree with the first segment of `domain`.

version.description: Bumped when case ids are renamed or removed (breaking for consumers).

description.description: What this domain covers, and where its boundary is.

allOf.$comment: Cases about something going wrong must say what going wrong looks like, and must pose the question a developer should be asked. Happy-path and contract cases state behaviour instead, so both fields are optional there.

id.description: Stable identifier, e.g. auth.token.expires-mid-request. Never reuse after removal.

title.description: One line, states the situation — not the fix.

category.description: The kind of behaviour this case pins down. A feature's spec needs all of them, not only the ones where it breaks: happy-path (it does the thing), contract (response shape, status, ordering), boundary (empty/one/huge/past-the-end), state-transition (what a change does to existing state), race, failure, security, data-integrity, ux. Retrieval balances across these so no single kind fills the result.

risk.description: Impact if unhandled, not likelihood of occurring. `foundational` marks behaviour the feature is defined by — a happy-path or core contract case that belongs in every spec regardless of risk appetite, and that retrieval always returns first.

applies_when.description: Context gates. Retrieval uses these to stay relevant.

question.description: The question a careful engineer would ask before writing the code.

why.description: Why this is missed. The mechanism, not the restated question.

observable.description: Measurable correct behaviour. Assertions derive from this field.

automatable.description: Whether a test can assert this unattended. `no` cases surface as manual notes.

related.description: Case ids that this one tends to pull in.

source.description: Specific citation: spec clause, documented behaviour, postmortem, or first-hand bug.

verified.description: true only once a human has opened the source and confirmed it says this. LLM-drafted entries stay false.
